steps.description:
Create a program that does the following: 1. Asks user to input a question in the format: "what is string?" string is a word and must be followed by "?". 2. Display string.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

what is blobfish?

what is axolotl?

what is okapi?

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input: what is blobfish? blobfish

Example 2 Input: what is axolotl? axolotl

Example 3 Input: what is okapi? okapi

Create a program that does the following: 1. Asks user to input 2 words separated by space. 2. if both words are the same, display "match". 3. Else if one word is a substring of the other, display "similar". 4. Otherwise, display "different".

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

cat fish

catfish fish

fish fish

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 2 words: cat fish different

Example 2 Input 2 words: catfish fish similar

Example 3 Input 2 words: fish fish match

Create a program that does the following: 1. Asks user to input a word and append it to a word list if it is not "end". 2. Repeat step (1) until "end" is entered. 3. Asks user to input a search string. 4. If an exact match is found, display "match". 5. Else if search string is a substring of any string in the list, display "similar to string" (e.g. if "apple" exists in "pineapple", display "similar to pineapple") 6. Otherwise, display "not found". 7. Repeat steps (3) to (6) until "end" is entered.

Assume that any match found first in the record is taken as the result.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

basketball football baseball ball end volleyball baseball ball foot ketball end

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the example below:

Input word: basketball Input word: football Input word: baseball Input word: ball Input word: end Input search: volleyball not found Input search: baseball match Input search: ball match Input search: foot similar to football Input search: ketbal similar to basketball Input search: end

What differentiates an Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm from others is that the algorithm can be 'trained' with data and its responses will be affected by the information that it has 'learnt'. It can eventually suggest answers to questions that have never been presented to it before by generalising from what it has already learnt. For example, when you show a kid different pictures of a white cat and tell him it is a cat, eventually, he can tell you a black cat is also a cat because he draws the information from other features of the cat.

Hence, such AI algorithms have main 4 parts: 1. Input training data 2. Learn data 3. Generalise from data (the intelligence) 4. Suggest answers to questions

In this exercise, we will simulate a very simple AI (note that this is not the real AI engine works).

Write a program that performs the following: 1. Asks user for an input. User can input in 3 ways: "what is string?" "string is a number" "string is a word" (e.g. "what is cat?", "3 is a number", "dog is a word", etc) 2. If the user enters "string is a number" or "string is a word", append the information to the record and display 'learning' on the screen. 3. If the user enters "what is string?", a. the program will check if the string is in its record. b. if the exact string is found, display the result "word" or "number". c. else if the string is substring of a record string (or vice versa), display the result "likely word" or "likely number". d. else display "idk" (I don't know). 4. Repeat step (1) to (3) until user enters "end".

Assume that any match found first in the record is taken as the result.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input catfish is a word 34 is a number what is 34? what is catfish? what is 3? what is fish? what is 234? what is cattail? what is 5? 5 is a number what is 500? end

Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the example below:

Input: catfish is a word learning Input: 34 is a number learning Input: what is 34? number Input: what is catfish? word Input: what is 3? likely number Input: what is fish? likely word Input: what is 234? likely number Input: what is cattail? idk Input: what is 5? idk Input: 5 is a number learning Input: what is 500? likely number Input: end
